checks.name: capture-time-is-the-transaction-authority-time
checks.summary: A4, first verdict: PASSED. Capture sets CapturedAt from transactionAuthorityTime(ctx, u) -- the accessor Service.record (service.go:1638) also uses for every Event's At, declared once at internal/application/runner_version.go:315 and now called from both sites, so there is exactly ONE accessor in the package. It is NOT a second s.clock.Now() call. Measured: the stored CapturedAt equals the At of the single requirement.captured event recorded by the same operation, compared value to value on Equal AND on Unix seconds AND on nanoseconds AND on location name, and equals the injected clock's instant exactly. NOTE ON THE WORK ORDER's LINE NUMBERS: A4 cites service.go:1386-1393 for the accessor; measured, Service.record is at service.go:1638 and the shared accessor is at runner_version.go:315. The cited lines are stale; the accessor is the one A4 describes.

checks.name: capture-time-is-stable-across-a-transaction-retry
checks.summary: A4, retry verdict: PASSED, UNCHANGED ACROSS 4 ATTEMPTS. The retry is driven at the seam the Firestore adapter actually retries at: a Transactor decorator runs the caller's callback in full and aborts it three times, then runs it a fourth time for real, passing the SAME context each attempt -- which is the mechanism, because Service.mutate reads the clock ONCE before Transact and puts the value on the context. A spy UnitOfWork records the CapturedAt staged on every attempt: all 4 are identical on Equal, on Unix seconds and on nanoseconds, the committed value equals them, and exactly one Requirement and one event are committed, so the aborted attempts leaked nothing. The Firestore adapter's own CONTENTION retry is recorded as not driven in the skips entry below, with its reason.

checks.name: neither-read-time-nor-event-scan
checks.summary: A5, all four parts PASSED. (1) Reading the same Requirement through two Services with DIFFERENT injected clock instants (1700000000 and 1900000000) produces byte-identical marshalled responses, and the reported captured_at equals neither read time. (2) The identical record read from a store whose event log is EMPTY reports the identical capture time, so no derivation from events is possible; the comparison store is asserted to have at least one event and the emptied one exactly zero, so the check cannot pass vacuously. (3) An AST scan over capturedAtView asserts its parameter is domain.Requirement and that its body mentions NO identifier that is not a parameter, a local, or predeclared -- no imported package, no package-level state, no clock. The matcher is verified FIRST: a known-negative helper that reads only its parameter reports no external names, and a known-positive helper that calls time.Now() reports 'time'. (4) An AST scan over EVERY non-test file in the package finds exactly three CapturedAt write sites and classifies them by their value expression: two read-model projections from capturedAtView, both in readmodels.go, and exactly ONE domain write, in service.go's Capture, whose value is the local capturedAt -- which the same test proves is bound from a call to transactionAuthorityTime. The scan additionally asserts that Capture's transaction callback contains ZERO 'Now' selectors, so nothing inside the part Firestore may retry reads a clock.

checks.name: legacy-record-omits-the-key-entirely
checks.summary: A6, verdict: THE KEY IS OMITTED, NOT EMITTED AS THE ZERO INSTANT. For a Requirement with a zero CapturedAt, RequirementDetailView.CapturedAt and RequirementView.CapturedAt are both nil, and the MARSHALLED BYTES of the detail view, the list row and the whole page were scanned: none contains the string 'captured_at' and none contains the literal '0001-01-01'. A recorded record's detail view does contain 'captured_at', so the absence is a statement about the value and not about the marshaller. The same scan at the HTTP boundary is green in internal/api for GET /v1/requirements and GET /v1/requirements/{id}. capturedAtView returns nil for a legacy record and a COPY for a recorded one: writing through the returned pointer and re-reading leaves both the view and the stored Requirement unchanged. MEASURED AND RECORDED HONESTLY, because it is a real distinction: the PERSISTED Firestore payload for a Requirement whose CapturedAt is zero DOES carry "CapturedAt":"0001-01-01T00:00:00Z", which is what json.Marshal does with a zero time.Time and which omitempty cannot suppress (dp-v2-073 d2 says so). A6 constrains the READ VIEW, and the read view omits the key, so no consumer is ever handed the zero instant; a document written BEFORE the field existed carries no key at all and reads back as a legacy record, asserted on both adapters.

checks.name: persistence-in-both-stores
checks.summary: A10: ONE behavioural table with the SAME NAME in both adapters -- TestRequirementCaptureTimeBehaviouralTable and TestRequirementCaptureTimeRollbackLeaksNothing exist in both internal/store/memory and internal/store/firestore with the same four cases. All four passed on Firestore against the local emulator (verdict line: ok .../internal/store/firestore 0.707s; subtests 0.49s / 0.05s / 0.02s / 0.13s) and on the memory adapter (ok .../internal/store/memory 0.005s): (1) a captured Requirement round-trips its capture time unchanged, compared on Equal and on the seconds/nanoseconds representation; (2) a rolled-back transaction leaks no capture time into committed state, including an attempt to MOVE an already-committed record's capture time, which is rolled back with its version; (3) a document written before the field existed reads back as a LEGACY RECORD rather than an error -- on Firestore the payload is built field by field WITHOUT the key (asserted not to contain 'CapturedAt', since marshalling a zero-valued Requirement would emit the key and test a different case) and written through writeRawFields; (4) the value is unchanged by every lifecycle transition applied through the service, driven as Capture followed by two Plans, with the version bump and the increment count asserted first so the capture-time assertion cannot be vacuous. NEITHER internal/store/memory/store.go NOR internal/store/firestore/store.go WAS EDITED, and neither needed to be: both are absent from git diff --cached, so the design's claim that the existing plain json.Marshal and state.clone() already carry the field is confirmed by measurement and no escalation was required. An AST test in internal/application pins that Capture and Plan are the COMPLETE set of service functions calling SaveRequirement, which is what makes case (4) exhaustive rather than a sample.

checks.summary: Gate rule G7, every skip recorded and NONE counted as a pass. (1) internal/store/firestore's integration tests, including this task's two new ones, call t.Skip when FIRESTORE_EMULATOR_HOST is unset -- verdict line without the emulator: ok .../internal/store/firestore 0.012s with the cases SKIPPED, which is why every Firestore claim in this record is backed by the separate emulator run recorded in the persistence-in-both-stores check (scripts/firestore-emulator.sh, all four cases PASS). Reason: a real contention retry requires two concurrent transactions, and the repository's determinism rule forbids a goroutine in a test; forcing one would also make the number of attempts a race rather than a fixed number. A4 permits recording it as skipped with its reason, and the retry-stability property is instead driven deterministically at the same seam the adapter retries at -- the transaction callback, re-invoked with the same context -- which is recorded as PASSED with 4 attempts in the capture-time-is-stable-across-a-transaction-retry check.
